purpose: Validate/correct the 8 provisional SA growing zones so a farm site (monthly temp/rain, frost, Koppen, elevation — the shape lib/site-climate.ts's SiteClimate already carries) can be auto-classified into one. Classification rules below are written on THAT data shape, and wherever possible reuse the app's own already-audited thresholds (lib/koppen-global.ts) rather than inventing new ones, per the brief's instruction to read how site climate is derived first.

appDataFields.note: Fields available on lib/site-climate.ts's SiteClimate + the MonthlyClimate it feeds classifyKoppen()/rainPatternFor() with.
derivable: summerRainShare = sum(rain Oct-Mar)/annualMm for southern hemisphere (koppen-global.ts summerMonthIndices)
elevation NOT in SiteClimate today — a gap, see below

zones.name: Highveld
zones.provinces: Gauteng, Free State, North West, Mpumalanga highveld (Witbank/Middelburg/Dullstroom/Belfast/Lydenburg/Harrismith)
zones.description: Cold, summer-rain interior plateau with real hard/regular winter frost.

classificationRules.coldestMonthMeanC: < 13, typically 6-11 (Bloemfontein ~8C, Johannesburg ~10C per app's own cited readings)
classificationRules.elevationBand_m: ~1200-1800 (GAP: no elevation figure in SiteClimate to check this against; see gaps)
classificationRules.appRainPatternResult: 'summer' — koppen-global.ts's rainPatternFor: summerShare>=0.65 and coldest-month <13C fails the >=13C light-frost carve-out, so it falls to 'summer'.

frostWindow.notes: 'real hard frost risk May-Aug' per the catalog's own header

zones.plantingSeasonNotes: Transplant/sow warm-season crops Oct-Nov once frost risk passes.

evidence.quote: The Highveld, known for its frost-prone winters and cooler spring temperatures, has a narrower window for successful planting, with the ideal time to transplant seedlings from October to November. Planting earlier risks exposure to late frost.
evidence.doc: Starke Ayres, 'Pinpointing the Best Green Pepper Planting Season in South Africa by Region', 3 Nov 2025

zones.name: Karoo / Arid Interior
zones.provinces: Northern Cape, Great/Upper Karoo, Little Karoo, Kalahari, Namaqualand (De Aar, Colesberg, Kimberley, Upington, Springbok, Sutherland, Kakamas, Pofadder)

classificationRules.note: Aridity (group B) is checked FIRST in classifyKoppen and overrides the temperature/rain-seasonality logic that assigns the other 7 zones — an arid-interior site should be routed to karoo-arid on koppen.group==='B' before any of the summer/winter/frost checks below are applied.
classificationRules.appRainPatternResult: rainPatternFor explicitly special-cases group B in its own mild-frost carve-out ('Arid (group B) is excluded... Upington frosts with a coldest month near 11-13C, so the mean alone cannot clear it of frost'), i.e. arid sites can still return 'summer' even with a mild-looking coldest-month mean.

zones.plantingSeasonNotes: Almost entirely irrigation-dependent; dryland cropping marginal.

evidence.quote: Arid (group B) is excluded: a desert's clear winter nights fall far below its monthly mean (Upington frosts with a coldest month near 11-13 °C), so the mean alone cannot clear it of frost.

zones.name: High Mountain
zones.provinces: Drakensberg, Lesotho border (Matatiele, Sterkspruit, Mount Fletcher), NE Free State highlands (Harrismith area), EC highlands
zones.description: Severe frost, short growing season, alpine/highland grassland — a small-area zone that commercial seed-company region tables typically fold into a neighbouring lowland region (see mergeSplitSuggestions), but which a vegetation/Köppen study keeps distinct.

koppen: Cwc (subtropical highland, short summer — 0.31% of SA's area per Conradie's Table 3, consistent with a small alpine extent)
classificationRules.note: South Africa's Köppen inventory (Conradie 2012, Table 3) contains NO snow (D) or polar (E) classes at all — everything sums to A+B+C = 100%. The country's most extreme cold-and-short-season areas therefore present as Cwc, not as a D-class, under the standard Köppen scheme; a site-climate classifier should not expect to see group D/E for a South African coordinate.
classificationRules.appRainPatternResult: Not distinctly handled by rainPatternFor today — a Cwc site with summer-dominant rain and a low coldest-month mean would currently fall out as 'summer', identical to highveld. Flagged as a gap: the app has no elevation input to separately route high-mountain sites.

frostWindow.notes: Longest and severest frost window of the 8 zones — GAP: no primary-sourced first/last-frost dates found this pass

zones.plantingSeasonNotes: Very short frost-free window; GAP — no region-specific sowing chart found.

mergeSplitSuggestions: Kirchhoffs' own 8-region commercial table does not map 1:1 onto the brief's 8 zones: it splits the interior hot lowland into 'Middleveld/Bushveld' + 'Lowveld' (both = this file's single lowveld-bushveld), and it merges western-cape + southern-cape into one 'Western and Southern Cape' row despite their different rain seasonality (Csb winter-dominant vs Cfb all-year) — evidence above. Recommend KEEPING western-cape and southern-cape split in the app, since rainPatternFor already produces different RainPatterns for them (winter vs all-year) from real seasonality data; a commercial guide's convenience grouping is not a climatic argument for merging.

No source found gives high-mountain its own commercial planting table — Kirchhoffs folds Drakensberg-border towns (Matatiele, Mount Fletcher, Sterkspruit) into 'Eastern Cape & Little Karoo'. However Conradie's vegetation-based regional map (Fig 1: 'Eastern Mountain grassland', 'Alpine Heathland') and its Köppen table (a distinct, small-area Cwc class) both support keeping high-mountain as its own zone for classification purposes, just accepting that no seed-company sowing chart will ever name it directly — its planting notes will stay a GAP until a DAFF/ARC source is reached.

CORRECTION to the brief's own rain-pattern write-up: BRIEF.md's 'all-year' definition lists 'Lowveld' alongside KZN/EC coast, but the app's own rainPatternFor (as audited in koppen-global.ts, citing Mkuze at ~80% summer rain / 17C coldest month) computes 'mild-frost' for real Lowveld coordinates, not 'all-year' — summer rain in the Lowveld is too seasonally concentrated (>=65% Oct-Mar) to clear the 0.35-0.65 band that 'all-year' requires. Recommend treating lowveld-bushveld as mild-frost, matching the code, not the brief's prose list.
